hints: Notice the $60.0^\circ$ in the diagram is between the two first order beams, not between one beam and the central normal.
Recall the grating equation $d \sin \theta = n\lambda$ uses $\theta$ measured from the straight-through direction to one $n$th order maximum.
Connect $d = 1.15 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and $n=1$ with $\theta = 30.0^\circ$ to calculate $\lambda$, then convert to $\text{nm}$.
walkthrough: The grating equation is $d \sin \theta = n\lambda$, where $\theta$ is the angle of the $n$th order maximum from the central axis.
The diagram shows $60.0^\circ$ between the upper and lower first order beams, so by symmetry each beam is at $\theta = 60.0^\circ / 2 = 30.0^\circ$ to the incident light direction.
Convert to nanometres: $5.75 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 575 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 575 \text{ nm}$. This is option C.

options.A: Gives half the correct value, from dividing by $n=2$ instead of $n=1$ for first order maxima.
options.B: Comes from halving $\sin 60.0^\circ$ instead of halving the $60.0^\circ$ angle to get $\theta$.
options.D: Comes from using the full $60.0^\circ$ between the beams as $\theta$ in $d \sin \theta = \lambda$.
